<STRUCT_0001><STRUCT_0002>
The reason for these choices is that we want to clearly distinguish between
the different types of objects in this chapter, to build the foundations.

<STRUCT_0001>
Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme contained in <MATH_0002>.
The basic object of study in this chapter will be a
category fibred in groupoids
<MATH_0003>, see
Categories, Definition <REF_0001>.
We will often simply say ``let <MATH_0004> be a category fibred
in groupoids over <MATH_0005>'' to indicate
this situation. A <MATH_0006>-morphism <MATH_0007> of categories
fibred in groupoids over <MATH_0008> will be a <MATH_0009>-morphism
in the <MATH_0010>-category of categories fibred in groupoids over
<MATH_0011>, see
Categories,
Definition <REF_0002>.
It is simply a functor <MATH_0012> over
<MATH_0013>.
We recall this is really a <MATH_0014>-category and that all <MATH_0015>-fibre products
exist.
